name: Viking
notes: Built by Silo AI with TurkuNLP (University of Turku) and HPLT; released before the AMD acquisition.

name: Bielik v3
notes: Depth up-scaled from Mistral 7B v0.2, then continued pre-training (v3 technical report). v3.1 (Nov 2026) continues the v3 line with 500B more tokens of multilingual pre-training (32 to 56 languages), SFT on 26M samples and RL (modified GRPO) in 14 environments; its added data and any teacher models are not described. Teachers listed come from the v3.0 report. The card still links the v3 AI Act summary, whose bielik.ai link returned a 404 page on 2026-11-12.

name: Poro 2
notes: Built by AMD Silo AI with TurkuNLP.

name: Gemma 4
notes: First Gemma generation under plain Apache 2.0 (earlier Gemma used the Gemma Terms of Use + Prohibited Use Policy). Card names data categories only (web, code, math, images, audio; cutoff Jan 2025). Pre-trained on TPUv4/TPUv6e. 35+ languages supported, 140+ in pre-training, no list given. AI Act summary seen only via AIAL tracker; primary URL not located.

name: gpt-oss
notes: Apache 2.0 plus a one-sentence USAGE_POLICY file (comply with applicable law). Text-only pre-training data "with a focus on STEM, coding, and general knowledge", cutoff June 2024. 2.1M H100-hours for 120b. AIAL lists gpt-oss among models whose mandatory AI Act summary could not be found.

name: Phi-4-Reasoning-Vision
notes: MIT. SFT of Phi-4-Reasoning (itself from Phi-4) with Google SigLIP-2 vision encoder (mid-fusion). 240 B200 for 4 days; Phi-4 base pre-trained on 1920 H100. DATACARD.md is the EU AI Act public summary (Microsoft Ireland). Primarily English; not intended for multilingual use.

name: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5
notes: Licence switched to OpenMDW-1.1 (Linux Foundation, MIT-style permissive model licence) for Nemotron 3.5. Lightning 30B-A3B is developed from NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B (AI Act summary; family base_model); Super VL 120B-A12B is initialised from Nemotron 3 Super Base (model override). Both are distilled for 1T tokens from the next-larger Nemotron 3 base (Super 3 Base for Lightning, Ultra 3 Base for Super), then trained further (long context on GB200 for Lightning, GB300 for Super). Pre-trained >20T tokens with NVFP4 recipe. Datasets largely released; purchased vendor data (Mercor, Turing, TAUS, Patronus) private. Post-training also used closed models (GPT-5.5; GPT-5.6 Sol, Gemini 3 Flash, GPT-4o mini and Claude 4 Sonnet for filtering) and Chinese open models incl. Kimi K3 and Qwen3.5.

name: Granite 4.2
notes: Apache 2.0. Post-trained (SFT + GRPO RL with NeMo RL/Gym) from Granite 4.1 base (from scratch, ~15T tokens, CommonCrawl ~59%). Machine-readable dataset disclosures (AIBOM JSON) on GitHub; many post-training sets are NVIDIA Nemotron datasets. Trained on NVIDIA GB200 NVL72 at CoreWeave (location not stated). AIAL lists Granite 4.2 AI Act summary as missing.

name: Olmo 3 / 3.1 Instruct
notes: Apache 2.0; Responsible Use Guidelines referenced as intent, not licence condition. Dolma 3 (pre/mid/long-context) and Dolci (post-training) released with code (OLMo-core, Open Instruct) and intermediate checkpoints. 1024 H100 cluster. Synthetic data from GPT-4.1, o4-mini, QwQ-32B, DeepSeek R1, Qwen3.

name: Qwen3.8 (Apache-2.0 open models)
notes: Card states Pre-training & Post-training and "built on the architectural foundation of Qwen3.5"; whether initialised from a Qwen3.5 checkpoint is not stated. No technical report or data section for Qwen3.8; the 2.4T-A95B flagship sits under a separate Qwen3.8-Max License.

name: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next
notes: Qwen Community License 1.0: commercial use by any Model-as-a-Service or AI-coding/office-assistant business needs a separate licence from Qwen (no revenue threshold); name display above 100M MAU or USD 20M monthly revenue. Tech report covers architecture and ablations, not the data mix. Experimental preview of the Qwen4 architecture.

name: DeepSeek-V4 (Pro)
notes: Pre-trained on more than 32T tokens; AI Act public summary covers DeepSeek-V4 (Pro and Flash): Common Crawl, Stack Exchange, licensed data, own synthetic data, no user data. Tech report validates inference on NVIDIA GPUs and Huawei Ascend NPUs but does not name the pre-training hardware.

name: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash
notes: Trained from scratch on a 45T-token multimodal corpus (7:1 text to multimodal; Common Crawl re-bootstrapped). Final on-policy distillation uses over 40 teacher models that are not named. The AI Act summary found covers V4 only.

name: GLM-5.3
notes: Same base model as GLM-5.2; gains come from post-training only. GLM-5.3 License replaces the MIT licence of GLM-5.2: MaaS operators above USD 10B yearly revenue must pass a Z.ai security review whose scope Z.ai determines. Post-training data and teachers not documented.

name: GLM-5.3-Flash
notes: Newly trained base model (hybrid sparse and linear attention, mHC) on a 30T-token multimodal pre-training corpus; mix not described. Plain MIT licence.

name: Tencent Hy4
notes: Final release of the model first published as Hy4 preview: 770B-A49B MoE language backbone (Gated DeepSeek Sparse Attention, IndexCache, iHC), now with a 1.23B ViT for image and video input and a 3.3B DFly2 drafter; the pre-trained base is released as Hy4-base. No longer plain Apache-2.0. Tencent Hy License 1.0: the Apache-2.0 text plus Section 10, under which a Model-as-a-Service operator needs a separate written licence if its worldwide gross revenue exceeds USD 50M in any 12 months or for a product with more than 100M monthly active users; internal use is exempt. The grant is worldwide, without the territory exclusions of earlier Hunyuan community licences, and there is no use policy. The card says only that pre-training and post-training were scaled up from the preview; neither 'from scratch' nor the starting weights are stated, so origin is unknown. Pre-training data not described; the card names only synthetic instruction data in the base's mid-training (generating models not named), game-development data curated with Tencent's games group and finance workspaces and tasks built in-house. The Hy4 System Card on hy.tencent.ai could not be read (the site rejects automated requests). An AI Act summary exists for Hy3 only.

name: K-EXAONE 2.0
notes: Upcycled from K-EXAONE (48->78 layers, 128->256 experts), then continual pre-training, mid-training and post-training. GPUs provided by a Korean government programme; location and accelerator not stated. First EXAONE under Apache-2.0.

name: EXAONE 4.5
notes: Vision-language model: 1.2B vision encoder trained from scratch, attached to EXAONE 4.0 32B. EXAONE AI Model License 1.2 - NC prohibits commercial use and lets the licensor amend it at any time.

name: Solar Open 2
base_model: Solar Open 1 (selective weight transfer, 2.3% of weights)
notes: 250B-A15B hybrid linear-attention MoE, ~12T tokens. Initialised by selective transfer of 2.3% of Solar Open 100B weights, rest random (own lineage). Upstage Solar License = Apache-2.0 plus mandatory 'Solar' name prefix and 'Built with Solar'. Korean MSIT/NIPA GPU track, clusters by Lablup; location not stated.

name: HyperCLOVA X SEED Think
base_model: Qwen2.5-VL vision encoder (vision component only; language backbone pre-trained by NAVER)
notes: Language backbone pre-trained by NAVER (6T tokens in stage 1); vision encoder taken from Qwen2.5-VL, which the press says included its trained weights. Custom licence: commercial use allowed, extra terms above 10M MAU, binding AUP, NAVER may amend at any time.

name: LLM-jp-4.1 thinking
notes: Pre-training and mid-training 11.7T tokens; most of the corpus is published (some parts withheld for licensing reasons); SFT/DPO data published. SFT responses were regenerated with gpt-oss-120b. Trained on ABCI 3.0 (AIST, Japan).

name: Qwen3-Swallow v0.2
notes: CPT on 209.7B tokens (Japanese, English, math, code), then SFT and RLVR. Trained on ABCI 3.0 and TSUBAME4.0 (Japan). A technical paper was announced but not checked here.

name: GPT-OSS-Swallow v0.1
notes: CPT on 419.4B tokens, then SFT (gpt-oss-120b generated responses) and RLVR. Trained on ABCI 3.0 and TSUBAME4.0 (Japan).

name: PLaMo 3 NICT (2604)
notes: Base model only (not instruction-tuned); the instruct flagship PLaMo 3.0 Prime is closed-weight. The 31B was distilled from PFN/NICT's 120B (3T tokens), which is not released; the card does not say whether by pruning or logit distillation. Gated PLaMo Community License: commercial use only with registration and annual revenue <= JPY 1bn; PFN may amend.

name: Sarvam 30B / 105B
notes: MoE models trained from scratch (30B: 16T tokens, 105B: 12T tokens). Training entirely in India on IndiaAI Mission compute; GPU type not stated, NVIDIA contributed libraries. Hub metadata lists 'bo' (Tibetan); recorded as brx (Bodo), one of the 22 languages Sarvam names. Sarvam-105B-1711 (Nov 2026) keeps the Sarvam-105B base model and adds post-training for tool calling, instruction following, agentic tasks and Indian languages; that post-training data is not described.

name: Falcon-H1
notes: Hybrid attention/Mamba2. TII Falcon License: Apache-2.0-based with modifications and an Acceptable Use Policy that 'may be updated from time to time'. Synthetic rewrites by unnamed 'internal and external open models'.

name: Falcon-H1R
notes: Reasoning model: cold-start SFT on long reasoning traces plus GRPO RL on Falcon-H1-7B-Base. Report discusses teacher models for traces but does not name them.

name: K2-Horizon
notes: Released by MBZUAI's Institute of Foundation Models (IFM). Pretraining 15T tokens in two phases, then midtraining to 512K, RL experts merged, SFT. Data, xLLM training code, logs and intermediate checkpoints published. A Math-Reasoning subset is named 'math-thinking-qwen' but no teacher model is named explicitly. Tech report was still 'In Progress'.

name: Jamba2
notes: SSM-Transformer (Mamba) hybrid. Mid-training on 500B tokens, SFT, DPO, on-policy RL starting from Jamba 1.5 pre-training (also stated for the 3B dense model). AI21 announced in May 2026 it would halt Jamba development. Languages are the pretraining emphasis of the Jamba 1.5 base; Jamba2 itself names none.

name: Command A+
notes: Sparse MoE, 218B total / 25B active, text+image input. Cohere's first MoE model; the AI Act summary lists >10T text tokens and synthetic data from Command A and other internal models. Apache-2.0 on Hugging Face; Cohere's Usage Policy applies to Cohere-hosted deployments.

name: Tiny Aya
notes: 3.35B, pretrained on 6T tokens (public and proprietary sources, 70 languages) on 256 H100s; region-specialised variants (global, earth, fire, water). CC-BY-NC plus Cohere Labs Acceptable Use Policy; gated on the Hub.

name: OpenEuroLLM 9B (Prelude)
notes: Prelude: Qwen3-architecture dense 9B with OpenEuroLLM's own 256k tokenizer, pre-trained on Leonardo (CINECA) toward 10T tokens; the released SFT model builds on the iter_0124800 (~1T tokens, not cooled down) checkpoint, extended to 256K context on LUMI and SFT-tuned on LUMI (AMD MI250X). Pre-training data: public sets (DCLM, FinePDFs, HPLT 3.0, Nemotron-CC incl. translated variants, StarCoder, MegaMath...) with per-source token counts. SFT data: Tulu-3 commercial subset, EuroBlocks-SFT-Synthetic, Nemotron-Post-Training-v2 math (synthetic traces), generators not named by the provider.

name: PLLuM 12B 2512
notes: Continued pre-training of Mistral-NeMo-Base-2407 on Polish (+ ~20% English) data, then SFT and preference alignment. Mistral NeMo was co-developed by Mistral AI and NVIDIA. Shared AI Act summary (in Polish) covers all 2512 chat models.

name: Llama-PLLuM 2512
notes: Continued pre-training of Llama-3.1-70B (base Llama-PLLuM-70B-base-2508), then SFT and preference alignment. Llama 3.1 Community License with AUP. Shared AI Act summary with PLLuM 12B.

name: Teuken 7B v0.6
notes: CC-BY-NC-4.0 (v0.6 base and instruct); only the older Teuken-7B-instruct-commercial-v0.4 is Apache-2.0. Base trained from scratch for 6T tokens on JUWELS Booster; v0.4 was the same run at 4T tokens, continued to 6T with a continue-decay schedule.

name: BgGPT 3.0
notes: Continued pre-training of Gemma 3 on curated Bulgarian CommonCrawl (cutoff May 2025, ~23M docs, <40B tokens, rehydrated), SFT, then SLERP merge with Gemma 3 base and IT models. Vision tower appended unchanged (no multimodal training). Trained with Google GCP credits; region and accelerators not stated. Gemma Terms of Use.

name: GaMS3
notes: 3 CPT stages (~13B parallel, ~101B base, ~20B long tokens) with per-corpus token tables, 2 SFT stages, hyperparameters published. ~150k GPU h on EuroHPC LEONARDO, ~40k GPU h on NVIDIA DGX Cloud Lepton (location not stated), ~1k GPU h on faculty B200. Some corpora (legal, medical, national library OCR) not public. Gemma Terms of Use.

name: Llama-Krikri
notes: Continued pre-training on 91B tokens (upsampled to 110B; Greek 62%, English 23%, parallel 6%, math/code 9%) with named sources in the tech report (arXiv 2505.13772); Greek vocabulary extension. Two AWS p5e.48xlarge (16 H200), ~50 days, via GRNET/OCRE; AWS region not stated. Llama 3.1 Community License.

name: Llama 3.1 EstLLM 70B
notes: Card: continued pre-training of Llama 3.1 70B on ~60B tokens, then SFT and DPO; no mix, compute or teachers stated for the 70B. The cited paper (arXiv 2603.02041) covers only the 8B models: ENC/Cosmopedia/FineMath mix, LUMI (AMD MI250x), Gemma 3 27B synthetic SFT data. Llama 3.1 Community License.

name: AMALIA 0626
base_model: EuroLLM-9B (EuroLLM consortium, PT) - final pre-training phase redone
notes: Continued EuroLLM-9B pre-training (final phase modified, +5.8B tokens of filtered Arquivo.pt, context to 32k), then SFT and DPO. Trained on MareNostrum 5 (BSC) and Deucalion (MACC, PT), NVIDIA H100. SFT and DPO datasets and training code released; the processed Arquivo.pt pre-training data was not found published. Teacher list from the technical report (March 2026), which predates the 0626 release; the 0626 card defers to it. No AI Act summary found on card or amaliallm.pt.

name: Gervasio 70B PTPT
notes: Fine-tuned on Portuguese instruction sets (extraGLUE-Instruct, NatInst-PTPT, MMLU-PTPT, Wiki-PTPT; only extraGLUE-Instruct found public). Released under MIT, but the base is under the Llama 3.3 Community License, which requires redistribution with the Llama agreement and attribution; it requires its terms, "Built with Llama" and the use policy for derivatives, hence custom. Training details: technical report announced, not published. Compute and hardware not stated.

name: Latxa 3.1 Instruct v2
notes: Further trained on Latxa Corpus v2 (public on HF) starting from Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct; trained on Leonardo (CINECA, EuroHPC), 256 A100. Card: further training details to follow in a paper. The EMNLP 2025 paper (v1) used synthetic instructions sampled from the Llama 3.1 Instruct backbone; not confirmed for v2. Llama 3.1 Community License inherited.

name: NorOLMo 1.0
notes: Base model only (no instruct yet). Continued pre-training of OLMo-2-1124-13B on ~275B tokens (HPLT v3, FinePDFs, OLMo-Mix, Sami corpora, math/code), all public datasets; intermediate checkpoints published as branches. Compute site not stated on card (HPLT usually trains on LUMI, unconfirmed). Training code not found linked.

name: Velvet
notes: Trained from scratch on Leonardo (CINECA, Bologna): over 4T tokens in six languages, about 23% Italian, plus 400B code tokens; pretraining data described only as publicly available sources. The newer Velvet 25B (2025-10, all 24 EU languages) is not released as open weights.

name: FastwebMIIA
notes: Trained from scratch in Italy with an in-house tokenizer on about 3T tokens; the AI Act summary gives the mix (Common Crawl about 85%, RedPajama-v2, FineWeb-Edu, Wikipedia about 1%, licensed Italian editorial and statistical content).

name: Domyn Edge
notes: 4B dense (3.93B) transformer trained from scratch on 13T tokens in six stages, natively to 1M context (256k recommended), on Leonardo (CINECA) with EuroHPC AI Factories compute. Rolling release in three bundles: bundle 1 (2026-10-20) has the base, the SFT checkpoint, 14 intermediate checkpoints, the stage 1 pre-training mix (7.59T of 8.44T released; stack-edu code withheld for attribution) and the training code. Teacher models, the SFT mix and the remaining stage datasets come in bundle 2; the final post-trained model and tech report in November 2026. Data stays documented until most of the 13T tokens are published.

name: Velvet2
notes: Second Velvet generation, trained from scratch on Leonardo (CINECA, Bologna); the 3B text model on about 5T tokens 'collected from publicly available sources' (cutoff Dec 2025 to Jan 2026), no datasets named; reuses the Velvet-14B tokenizer, not its weights. Vision (SigLIP2 encoder) and Speech (Whisper Large v3 encoder) variants build on Velvet2-3B. No release announcement yet; quotes from the public model page (repo files gated).

name: Muse Spark
notes: Muse Model License (Oct 2026): MIT-style grant, but the Usage Policy is incorporated and attached as Exhibit A; "Built with Muse Spark Open" display duty for products and Derivatives (incl. models trained on outputs); Model-as-a-Service providers with more than USD 20M revenue in 12 months need a separate agreement with Meta. No MAU clause and no EU exclusion (unlike Llama 4); EU licensees contract with Meta Platforms Ireland. Pre-training stack rebuilt after Llama 4 (origin scratch per Meta; the 202,048-token vocabulary matches Llama 4, so the tokenizer is likely reused). Same base model as the closed Muse Spark 1.3 plus extra safety post-training. Data described by category only. Muse models trained on Prometheus (New Albany, Ohio). Meta's AI Act summary names Muse Spark, not Spark Open, hence unknown.

name: Muse Glimmer
notes: Plain Apache 2.0; USAGE_POLICY.md is not part of the licence. Dense 29.6B incl. 1.8B perception encoder, "distilled from Muse Spark" for on-device agents. Data described by category only; more than 100 languages, no list given. Muse models trained on Prometheus (Ohio). AI Act summary V1 of 10 Aug 2026.

name: Mistral Large 4
notes: Mistral Ecosystem Open-Weight License: modified MIT; a licensee (or affiliate) that operates a Model-as-a-Service business needs a separate commercial licence from Mistral before commercial use (internal use and use via Mistral products exempt), hence custom. Unlike Mistral Large 3 (Apache 2.0). Trained from scratch "in Europe" on "European infrastructure"; site and hardware not stated, so compute is recorded as europe rather than eu. 1T total / ~49B active MoE, text and image input. Data described by category (Common Crawl, public datasets, user data, third-party synthetic and curated data). Preview 2026-10-06, weights released 2026-10.

name: Comet
notes: CompactifAI compression of NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Super VL (124.5B to 61.1B parameters, 12.3B active): expert pruning (512 to 256 routed experts per MoE layer) and a smaller expert intermediate size, then healing by distillation from the original Nemotron, which writes the training responses, and GRPO-style RL. Healing data described by category only; compute location not stated. OpenMDW-1.1 per card metadata and licence section (same as the base); the card's Model Information table still names the NVIDIA Nemotron Open Model License.

name: Kimi K3.1
notes: Post-trained from Kimi K3 (own, natively multimodal, pre-trained by Moonshot) with large-scale joint RL across hundreds of domains; first model of the K3.1 series. Not post-training only: the full-attention Gated MLA layers of K3 are replaced with Gated DeepSeek Sparse Attention layers, and the blog describes a mid-training stage from which cyber-related data was removed. No K3.1 report; data and teachers not named. Kimi K3.1-Pro License: same terms as the Kimi K3 License (MaaS operators above USD 20M yearly revenue need a separate agreement; name display above 100M MAU or USD 20M monthly revenue).

name: MiniMax-M3.1
notes: Presented as a next-generation Flash model "building on MiniMax-M3": keeps M3's MoE architecture (about 428B-A23B), replaces the first three full-attention layers with MiniMax Sparse Attention, adds quantization-aware training (NVFP4 experts, MXFP8 attention) and a DSpark draft head. Whether training started from M3's weights, and which stages ran, is not stated, so origin stays unknown. No M3.1 data description or AI Act summary found (the M3 summary names MiniMax-M3 only). MiniMax Community License as for M3, now "Built with MiniMax M3.1-Flash": non-commercial by default; commercial use needs attribution and a notice, prior written authorisation above USD 20M yearly revenue; prohibited uses include any military purpose.

name: LongCat-2.5
notes: Native multimodal MoE with discrete visual tokens; card and blog say it builds on LongCat-2.0 but not whether it starts from its weights (the configs share the same backbone). Mid-training and SFT with long sequences, agentic RL, multi-teacher on-policy distillation from in-house domain experts; an unnamed LLM judge audits RL trajectories. Pre-training data not described. Trained on domestic Chinese AI accelerators (vendor not named). Plain MIT licence.

name: Ling-3.1-flash
notes: 560B-A25B hybrid-linear MoE (KDA + Gated MLA), hybrid reasoning. AI Act public summary: more than 10T text tokens; Common Crawl, other public datasets by category, licensed data, own crawler (Ant Spider), synthetic data from Ling-2.6 models, no user data; model dependencies NA. Card says it builds upon the smaller Ling-3.0-flash (124B-A5.1B). MIT in card metadata; no LICENSE file in the repo.

name: ERNIE 5.5 Flash
notes: Base model only: the checkpoint at the end of pre-training, before any mid- or post-training; the post-trained ERNIE 5.5 Flash is announced, not released. 280B-A14B MoE (MLA with sparse attention plus Heavily Compressed Attention, Multi-Router Latent MoE, mHC), 33.5T tokens. ERNIE 5.5 Flash Base Model License v1.0 grants no rights in the EU, the UK or South Korea (excluded from the 'Territory'; use outside it is not authorised). Commercial use free up to USD 50M related annual revenue with a one-time notice and 'Powered by ERNIE', above that only with written authorisation; outputs may not be used to improve other models; the Acceptable Use Policy (Exhibit A, part of the licence) may be revised. Pre-training data described by category only; quality filtering by unnamed models.

name: Olala v1.0 mini
notes: Hybrid Mamba-3/attention latent MoE (6.77B total, about 1B active) by OVHai LLM (OVH LLM SAS, OVHcloud group). The base was pre-trained from scratch on 12.8T tokens (10.4T pre-training, 2.38T annealing) on 1,024 GH200 GPUs of JUPITER (Jülich, EuroHPC); SFT (162B trained tokens) and a four-stage GRPO RL cascade ran on H100 GPUs of Jean Zay, a smaller DGX cluster (location not stated) and MeluXina. Qwen tokenizer reused (151,936 entries; tokenizer only, attributed in NOTICE). The pre-training and annealing mixes are listed per source with token counts (FineWeb-2, Nemotron-CC v2, Nemotron code and math sets, CCMatrix, ParaCrawl ...); only parts of the public sets were used and the mixed corpus is not published. Three in-house synthetic datasets are public (Math-Enrich-Multilingual, Wikipedia-ActiveReading, ProofWiki-ActiveReading), although the base AI Act summary calls them unpublished. SFT and RL data are given by group; the 27 SFT datasets and 89 RL sources are not listed. One AI Act summary per repo (base, SFT, final). A 256k context extension (Jean Zay) is described but not released.

name: Munin 2.0
notes: Post-training of NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Super Base with architecture and tokenizer unchanged: SFT on LUMI (one epoch, 6.8M conversations, 11B tokens, 16 nodes with AMD MI250X), then RL with asynchronous GRPO on Gefion (DGX H100; about 119,000 episodes from 22 task sources, rewards from programs only, sandboxes on Hetzner). SFT data: about 94% of the trained tokens from public datasets, 6% synthetic data DFM generated, 8% Danish and 9% mixed Danish/English; the list of about 100 sources and the AI Act training summaries are announced for later. RL sources are named (Scale-SWE, SWE-smith, OpenSWE, Terminal-Lego, TMax and others) and the RL setup is in DFM's prime-rl fork. Compute is where DFM's post-training ran; NVIDIA's pre-training site is not stated. Released under the base model's NVIDIA Nemotron Open Model License (attribution notice, indemnity, US export clause; fixed version of 2025-12-15). DFM states it is not the provider of a new GPAI model (about 0.25% of the compute threshold). Hosted by the Alexandra Institute within DFM.

name: DFM Mimir v1.8
notes: HRM-Text recurrent architecture (XL: about 1B non-embedding, 1.79B total parameters), PrefixLM, Gemma 4 tokenizer (tokenizer only, no Gemma weights). Same XL run as v1 (from scratch, step 1.65M) and v1.5 (step 2,877,261), continued through the DFM12 to DFM15 mixtures, which extend the data to 50 languages, to step 3,800,000; final mixture DFM15 (MTC v1.8). Training sources other than the agreement-backed DBC and Lex.dk material are pinned public Hub packages with rebuild scripts in the HRM-Text repo; the card states that public downloads alone cannot reconstruct that material. The card names no languages (tag: multilingual), no compute site and no developers; site and hardware (UCloud at SDU, 8 B200) are stated for v1 and v1.5. No AI Act summary published (a draft for v1, marked not for publication, is in the HRM-Text repo).

name: Latxa 3
notes: Basque adaptation of the post-trained Qwen3.5-122B-A10B following the recipe of Sainz et al. (EMNLP 2025): the instruct backbone is trained further on the Basque corpus together with instruction data. The best configuration from experiments on smaller Qwen3.5 models was applied to three models; the 122B-A10B received an additional training pass. Trained on Latxa Corpus v2 (public on the Hub, since 2026-02-13 in a curated version with some data removed for permission compliance) on MareNostrum 5 (BSC; EuroHPC AI Factory project led by EJIE with HiTZ), up to 256 H100. The instruction data and who generated its reasoning traces are not stated; a paper is in preparation. Apache-2.0, like the base model. The card calls the earlier Latxa Llama 3.1 70B Instruct v2 'Latxa 2'.

name: EuroLLM 1.5
notes: Released without documentation of its making: the cards give evaluation results only and ask to cite the EuroLLM-22B report 'until the EuroLLM1.5 technical report is released'. Not stated: whether 1.5 was trained from scratch or continues EuroLLM-9B (the config has the same shape and the tokenizer files are identical to EuroLLM-9B-2512), training data, compute site, teacher models. The consortium's AI Act summary (v1.0, 2026-07-31) lists the 9B and 22B models, not 1.5. The instruction-tuned EuroLLM1.5-9B-SFT is a preview release without a licence and is not listed. Languages from the Hub metadata of the base model.

name: Villanova2
notes: Second Villanova generation (IPCEI-CIS Villanova project): sparse MoE on a Qwen3-Next hybrid architecture (Gated DeltaNet plus attention) with its own 131k BPE tokenizer, pre-trained from scratch on 4.7T tokens in one run (4.0T stable, 600B annealing, 100B long context) on 64 NVIDIA B200 GPUs; where the cluster is located is not stated ('Built in EU, for EU'). Pre-training sources named per stage (FineWeb-Edu, DCLM-Edu, FinePDFs, FineWeb-2, FineWeb2-HQ, FineWiki, FineMath, Nemotron-CC, Stack-Edu, Common Pile, Dolma 3 and others), without shares. Post-training: SFT on 3.68M conversations (10.87B tokens), DPO on 275,516 pairs, GRPO; sources listed per domain, synthetic data only from permissively licensed models, DPO completions from unnamed open-weight models. Technical report announced ('Coming soon'). The vision-language variants use Qwen3.5-122B-A10B for generated text.

name: Embla 1
base_model: Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-Base (Alibaba, CN): embeddings and output head start from its top principal components
notes: Own architecture for phones (MoE with 8 of 96 routed experts, sparse ReLU-squared attention, shared K/V caches, a 3B-parameter n-gram 'engram' table): 10B total, 1B active. Pre-trained on 1.4T tokens with logit distillation from Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-Base from the first step; embeddings and output head start from the teacher's top principal components, the tokenizer is Qwen3.8's pruned to 65,536 tokens. Then 20B tokens to 256K context, SFT on 123B tokens with quantization-aware training for 4 bit, on-policy distillation, GRPO and multi-teacher distillation. Data given as category shares only (web text 50%/43%, code 19%, synthetic STEM 10%, math, PDFs, 5% multilingual web in 10 unnamed European languages); no datasets named. Trained on 16 nodes of 8 H100; the Gefion supercomputer (Denmark) is named by press, not in Sevren's own post. Origin is a judgement call: counted as partial weight transfer from a non-European model, not as distillation alone.

name: Lara Mini
notes: Base model only (7.2B total, 0.6B active MoE; hybrid of Gated DeltaNet, sliding-window and global attention), pre-trained from scratch on 6T tokens plus 100B for 128k context; uses the Qwen3 tokenizer, no Qwen weights. CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, commercial licences on request. Data: public datasets with tokens and shares per domain (English 41.4%, multilingual 36.4%, code 12.8%, math 5.9%, SFT-like 3.5%); 26% synthetic, mostly NVIDIA's Nemotron collections; no training data released. The card passes on use restrictions of the DeepSeek licence because of DeepSeek-generated synthetic data. Compute site not stated; the report acknowledges support from CINECA and the Horizon Europe project DVPS. Built as the general-purpose model underneath the Lara 4 translation system; the research page announces 'Lara 4 Mini and Lara Mini LLM' for December 2026.

name: Tencent Hy4 flash
base_model: SigLIP2-So400m-Patch16-Res512 vision encoder (Google; vision component only; language backbone pre-trained by Tencent)
notes: A separate model, not a variant of Hy4: 42-layer backbone (hidden size 3,072 against 6,144) with hybrid sparse and sliding-window attention, LatentMoE and n-gram (Engram) embeddings, pre-trained on its own (base released as Hy4-flash-base), then post-trained with self-distillation from Hy4 and RL. The origin value follows from the vision encoder, which the card says is adapted from SigLIP2-So400m-Patch16-Res512 (0.43B of 220B parameters); how the backbone was initialised is not stated. Pre-training data not described; synthetic instruction data in mid-training (generating models not named). Tencent Hy License 1.0, the same file as for Hy4: a Model-as-a-Service operator above USD 50M revenue or 100M monthly active users needs a separate written licence; no territory exclusion, no use policy. No System Card and no AI Act summary found for Hy4 flash.

name: Qwen-SEA-LION v5
notes: Qwen-based models of the SEA-LION v5 collection (397B Plus, 27B, 9B). Post-trained, text-only, on prompts from SEA-Instruct-2602: RL (GRPO-style policy gradient, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 as judge) and on-policy distillation from Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B in the same update. The 27B keeps Qwen's architecture unchanged; the 397B Plus was first converted to the Qwen4Exp architecture (model-level values). Training site and hardware not stated. Cards and metadata say MIT, while the LICENSE file in the repos is Qwen's Apache-2.0 text (Copyright Alibaba Cloud). The collection also holds Qwen-SEA-LION-v5-9B and, with Gemma 4 31B-IT as teacher, Gemma-SEA-LION-v5-E2B and Nemotron-SEA-LION-v5-E4B (not listed).

name: Inkling 2
notes: Apache 2.0 per card metadata (no LICENSE file in the repos, not gated) plus Thinking Machines' Model Acceptable Use Policy. The cards only link the policy, but the policy itself says that accessing, downloading or using the weights means agreeing to be bound by it, and that it can be updated at any time with continued use counting as acceptance; recorded as a binding policy on that wording, like the gpt-oss usage policy. Second generation after Inkling and Inkling-Small (July 2026): the AI Act summary of Inkling 2 Small says it was trained from scratch and only shares architectural approaches with them. Small: 8.4T tokens of initial pre-training (68 hours on NVIDIA GB300 NVL72) and 3.8T at 512K context, then two phases of reasoning and agent trajectories sampled from earlier models incl. Kimi K3 (about 320B and 34B tokens) and one joint RL run; trained natively in NVFP4. Mini is a separate 24-layer run on the same recipe: two thirds of its experts pruned in midtraining, then 1T tokens distilled from a larger internal Inkling model. Data by category only; Common Crawl is the one dataset named. Compute location not stated. The AI Act summary (Word file, 5 Nov 2026) covers Inkling 2 Small; none is listed for Mini. The card names English plus general multilingual ability; the summary says the training data covers all 24 official EU languages.

name: Aion 1.0
notes: MIT (plain LICENSE file; the card says nothing in it restricts or modifies the licence). Dense 2.3B model of the Windows Applied Sciences Group: replaces Phi-4-mini as the built-in model of Edge and is to replace Phi Silica in Windows, in a further optimised version, by the end of January 2027. Origin not stated: the card calls it a base model and describes its data as an extension of the Phi Silica data, without naming a base model or saying it was trained from scratch; a technical report is announced. Data by category only (filtered public documents and newly created synthetic data, about 6% multilingual); the generator of the synthetic data is not named. Compute and hardware not stated. No DATACARD.md or other AI Act training summary in the repo, unlike Microsoft's Phi models.

name: Kolibri 1.1
notes: Branches from the Kolibri 1 mid-training checkpoint at step 34,000 (20T pre-training and 3.42T mid-training tokens, trained from scratch), converts its attention to shared-KV sparse attention, then adds a second mid-training phase (805B tokens) and a long-context phase (201B tokens); SFT and RL are its own. The base is an intermediate checkpoint that was not released, and the AI Act summary states 'Model dependencies: None'. Training data, synthetic data and curation pipeline are those of Kolibri 1; the only new pre-training data is the reweighted mix of the second mid-training phase. The card gives GPU counts for the new phases (512 and 384) without site or accelerator type: the sites come from the Kolibri 1.1 blog post (Germany and Finland), the hardware from the Kolibri 1 card (768 NVIDIA B200 for the pre-training it continues).
